meaning_en: you say it when it is your time to play
meaning_es: lo dices cuando te toca jugar
scene: {A} holds the dice. {B} tries to grab it with both hands while a cat watches from the sofa.
bubble: "It's my turn!" shouts {A}. {B} hides behind a cushion.

options: Is my turn to throw the dice.
It's my turn to throw the dice.
It's my turn of throw the dice.
practice.why: The correct form is "It's my turn to + verb".

text: Can I have some water, please?
meaning_en: a polite way to ask for something
meaning_es: una forma educada de pedir algo
scene: {A} walks across the desert with a tiny glass. {B} appears from behind a cactus, holding an enormous jug.
bubble: "Can I have some water, please?" Splash! {B} gives {A} the whole jug.
example: Can I have a sandwich, please?

options: Can I have an apple, please?
Can I has an apple, please?
I can have apple, please you?

meaning_en: you say it when someone does something good
meaning_es: lo dices cuando alguien hace algo bien
scene: {A} stacks ten books on their head and walks across the room. {B} claps with a banana in each hand.
bubble: "Well done!" cheers {B}. Bananas fly everywhere.
example: Well done, you finished the puzzle!

options: Good done, you won the race!
Well done, you are lose the race!
Well done, you won the race!

meaning_en: you want to eat something
scene: {A} opens the fridge and a very tall sandwich falls on their head. {B} laughs and takes a photo.
bubble: "I'm hungry!" says {A}. Then the sandwich says "Me too!"

options: I'm hungry. Can I have a banana?
I have hungry. Can I have a banana?
I'm hungry. I drink a banana.
practice.why: We say "I am hungry", not "I have hungry".

meaning_en: a greeting for the start of the day
meaning_es: un saludo para empezar el día
scene: {A} runs into class in pyjamas and slippers. {B}, the teacher, drinks tea and does not even blink.
bubble: "Good morning, teacher!" {A} waves. {B} says, "Nice slippers."
example: Good morning, teacher! How are you?

options: Good night, teacher! The lesson is starting.
Good morning, teacher! The lesson is starting.
Good evening, teacher! It's eight in the morning.

meaning_en: a teacher's instruction to start reading
meaning_es: una instrucción de la profesora para empezar a leer
scene: {A} opens a book and a tiny dragon flies out. {B} closes the book very quickly and smiles.
bubble: "Open your book, please!" says {B}. {A}'s book roars.
example: Open your book, please. Go to page ten.

options: Open your book, please. Eat it on page ten.
Opening your book please, go to page ten.
Open your book, please. Go to page ten.
practice.why: We use "Open your book" to ask for the book to be opened.

meaning_en: you agree and say you have the same thing
meaning_es: dices que tú también tienes o quieres lo mismo
scene: {A} orders a pizza with chocolate. {B} stands up on a chair and shouts at the waiter.
bubble: "I love pizza!" "Me too!" Both dance on the table.
example: I like ice cream. Me too!

options: I like ice cream. Me neither!
I like ice cream. I too me!
practice.why: "Me too" agrees with a positive sentence.

meaning_en: you do not have the answer
scene: {A} asks a very old tortoise a very hard question. The tortoise thinks for a hundred years. {B} falls asleep.
bubble: "I don't know," says the tortoise. {B} wakes up angry.

meaning_en: a question to ask about feelings
meaning_es: una pregunta para saber cómo se siente alguien
scene: {A} greets a robot that is wearing sunglasses and a scarf. {B} presses its big red button.
bubble: "How are you today?" "Beep! Fantastic!" says the robot.
example: How are you today? I'm fine, thanks.

options: How you are today? I'm fine, thanks.
How are you today? I'm very well.
How is you today? Fine, thanks you.
practice.why: A question needs "How are you", not "How you are".

meaning_en: you ask someone to take a seat
meaning_es: le pides a alguien que se siente
scene: {A} is jumping on a chair like a frog. {B}, the teacher, points to a desk and waits.
bubble: "Sit down, please!" Boing! {A} lands on the desk instead.
example: Sit down, please. The lesson is starting.

options: Sit down, please. Here is your chair.
Sit on, please. Here is your chair.
Sit up, please. You are under the desk.
practice.why: The phrasal verb "sit down" means to take a seat.

meaning_en: you go from sitting to standing
meaning_es: pasar de estar sentado a estar de pie
scene: {A} sits on a whoopee cushion. {B} laughs and shouts at the whole class from the front.
bubble: "Stand up!" says {B}. The cushion goes PFFFT!

options: Stand up when the teacher comes in.
practice.why: "Stand up" is the opposite of "sit down".

meaning_en: you ask someone to see what is on the board
meaning_es: le pides a alguien que mire la pizarra
scene: {A} draws a huge sun on the board. {B} looks at the ceiling by mistake and sees a spider.
bubble: "Look at the board!" says {A}. "Look at the spider!" says {B}.

options: Look at the board. Read the first line.
Look to the board. Read the first line.
See at the board. Read the first line.
practice.why: We say "look at" when we turn our eyes to something.

meaning_en: you hear a word and say it too
meaning_es: escuchas una palabra y la dices también
scene: A parrot sits on {A}'s shoulder. {B} says "elephant" and the parrot says it back, but with a funny voice.
bubble: "Listen and repeat!" says {B}. "Elefant!" squawks the parrot.

practice.why: We say "Listen and repeat" for a pronunciation game.

text: Can I go to the toilet?
meaning_en: you ask the teacher for permission to leave
meaning_es: le pides permiso a la profesora para salir
scene: {A} crosses their legs and hops on one foot. {B}, the teacher, raises one eyebrow and points to the door.
bubble: "Can I go to the toilet?" asks {A}, hopping very fast.
example: Can I go to the toilet, please?

options: Can I going to the toilet, please?
Can I to go to toilet, please?
Can I go to the toilet, Miss?
practice.why: After "Can I" we use the base verb: "go".

meaning_en: a strong way to say thanks
meaning_es: una forma fuerte de dar las gracias
scene: {A} gives {B} a tiny flower. {B} bows ten times and gives {A} a huge cake in return.
bubble: "Thank you very much!" says {B}, with cream on their nose.
example: Thank you very much for the gift.

options: Thanks you very much for the gift.
Thank you very much for your help.
Thank you very much of the gift.

meaning_en: the answer when someone thanks you
meaning_es: la respuesta cuando alguien te da las gracias
scene: {A} carries a mountain of boxes for {B}. {B} says thank you, and {A} bows like a prince.
bubble: "Thank you!" "You're welcome!" says {A}, dropping the boxes.

meaning_en: you say it to get someone's attention politely
meaning_es: lo dices para llamar la atención con educación
scene: {A} wants to pass in a very full bus. {B} sits on three bags and does not hear anything.
bubble: "Excuse me!" says {A}. {B} jumps and gives away all three bags.
example: Excuse me, where is the library?

options: Excuse me, can I sit here?
Excuse I, where is the library?
Excusing me, where is the library?
practice.why: "Excuse me" is a polite way to start a question.

meaning_en: you say it when you did something wrong
meaning_es: lo dices cuando hiciste algo mal
scene: {A} kicks a ball. It flies through a window and lands in {B}'s soup. {B} looks up slowly.
bubble: "I'm sorry!" says {A}. {B} says, "The soup was cold anyway."
example: I'm sorry. I broke your pencil.

options: I'm sorry. I'm late for class.
I sorry. I broke your pencil.
practice.why: We say "I'm sorry" after a mistake.

meaning_en: you did not hear and ask the person to say it again
meaning_es: no escuchaste y pides que lo repitan
scene: {A} whispers a secret to a statue. {B} stands next to it, holding a big ear trumpet.
bubble: "Pardon?" says the statue. {B} nearly drops the trumpet.

options: Pardon? Can you say it again?
Pardon to me? Say it again.

meaning_en: you ask the name of a thing
meaning_es: preguntas el nombre de una cosa
scene: {A} finds a big green thing under the bed. {B} pokes it with a long stick.
bubble: "What's this?" asks {A}. The thing says, "I'm your sock!"

options: What this is? It's a pencil.
practice.why: We use "What's this?" for an object that is near.

meaning_en: you ask if something is a cat or not
meaning_es: preguntas si algo es un gato
scene: {A} sees a furry shape under a blanket. {B} peeks inside with a torch and screams softly.
bubble: "Is it a cat?" asks {A}. "It's my grandma's wig," says {B}.
example: Is it a cat? No, it's a dog.

options: It is a cat? Yes, it's.
Are it a cat? Yes, it is.
Is it a cat? Yes, it is.
practice.why: A question uses "Is it" at the start.

meaning_en: a short positive answer
scene: {A} asks a very sleepy owl, "Is it night?" The owl opens one eye. {B} holds a clock.
bubble: "Yes, it is," says the owl, and sleeps again. {B} tiptoes away.
example: Is it big? Yes, it is.

options: Is it red? Yes, it is.
Is it red? Yes, I is.
practice.why: Short answers do not use a contraction at the end.

meaning_en: a short negative answer
scene: {A} asks, "Is it a monster?" about a big shadow. {B} switches on the light and shows a small hat.
bubble: "No, it isn't!" laughs {B}. The hat blushes.
example: Is it hot? No, it isn't.

options: Is it hot? No, it isn't it.
Is it big? No, it isn't.
Is it big? No, it not.
practice.why: The negative short answer is "No, it isn't".

meaning_en: you say a food you enjoy
meaning_es: dices una comida que te gusta
scene: {A} dreams of a pizza as big as a car. {B} brings a ladder and eats the cheese from the top.
bubble: "I like pizza!" says {A}. {B} is already on the roof of it.
example: I like pizza and ice cream.

options: I am like pizza on Fridays.

meaning_en: you say you do not enjoy a food
meaning_es: dices que una comida no te gusta
scene: {A} sees a bowl of green soup with eyes. {B} steps back with a spoon in each hand.
bubble: "I don't like soup," says {A}. The soup says, "Neither do I."

meaning_en: you ask for help
scene: {A} is stuck in a box of balloons. {B} walks past with headphones and does not hear anything at first.
bubble: "Can you help me?" Pop! {B} sits on a balloon.

options: Can you help me with this bag?
practice.why: After "Can you" we use the base verb: "help".

meaning_en: you ask someone to move near you
meaning_es: le pides a alguien que se acerque
scene: {A} holds a banana in the air. A monkey sits far away. {B} tries to call it, and the monkey waves.
bubble: "Come here!" calls {B}. The monkey takes the banana and goes.
example: Come here and look at this.

options: Come to here and look at this.
Coming here and look at this.
Come here, please. I have a surprise.
practice.why: We use "come here" to ask someone to come near the speaker.

meaning_en: you suggest a game to your friends
meaning_es: propones un juego a tus amigos
scene: {A} finds a football in a field of sheep. {B} puts a sheep in goal. The sheep does not move.
bubble: "Let's play!" says {A}. "Baa," says the goalkeeper.

practice.why: After "Let's" we use the base verb.

meaning_en: you ask people not to leave without you
meaning_es: pides que no se vayan sin ti
scene: {A} runs after a school bus with one shoe on. {B} looks out of the window and waves with a sandwich.
bubble: "Wait for me!" Phew! {A} jumps in through the window.
example: Wait for me at the gate!

options: Wait to me at the gate!
practice.why: The phrase "wait for" needs the word "for".

meaning_en: you warn someone about danger
meaning_es: avisas a alguien de un peligro
scene: {A} carries a tower of ice creams across a muddy field. {B} sees a big puddle just ahead.
bubble: "Be careful!" cries {B}. Too late: {A} is now a snowman.
example: Be careful, the floor is wet.

options: Be careful with the hot tea.
Careful be, the floor is wet.
Are careful, the floor is wet.
practice.why: We use "Be careful" as a short command.

meaning_en: you tell someone to go faster
meaning_es: le dices a alguien que vaya más rápido
scene: {A} brushes their teeth very slowly. {B} stands at the door with a big bag and a nervous face.
bubble: "Hurry up!" says {B}. {A} answers, "I'm brushing the bear's teeth."
example: Hurry up! We're late for school.

options: Hurry up! The bus is here.
Hurry on! We're late for school.
Hurrying up! We're late for school.
practice.why: "Hurry up" is used to say "go faster".

meaning_en: you shout it to warn about danger
meaning_es: lo gritas para avisar de un peligro
scene: {A} paints a wall on a ladder. {B} sees a flying football coming straight at the paint pot.
bubble: "Look out!" Splash! {A} is now blue from head to toe.

options: Look out of! There's a car!
Look out! The ball is coming!

meaning_en: you want to drink something
scene: {A} walks out of the sports hall with a tongue as long as a scarf. {B} holds a tiny cup.
bubble: "I'm thirsty!" says {A}. {B} gives a cup the size of a thimble.
example: I'm thirsty. Can I have some juice?

options: I have thirsty. I want water.
I'm thirsty. I want some water.
I'm thirst. I want some water.
practice.why: We use "be" with "thirsty": I am thirsty.

meaning_en: you need to rest
scene: {A} yawns so wide that a bird flies into their mouth. {B} carries a pillow and a tiny bed.
bubble: "I'm tired," yawns {A}. The bird says, "Me too."
example: I'm tired. I want to go to bed.

options: I have tired after the long walk.
I'm tired after the long walk.
I'm tire after the long walk.

meaning_en: your body feels low temperature
scene: {A} wears three coats, two hats and a scarf. {B} offers a sock to put on their nose.
bubble: "I'm cold!" says {A}. Ice drips from their hat.
example: I'm cold. Can I have my coat?

options: I have cold. Please close the window.
I'm colding. Please close the window.
I'm cold. Please close the window.
practice.why: To say that you feel cold we use "I'm cold".

meaning_en: your body feels high temperature
scene: {A} sits in the sun, red like a tomato, with a fan in each hand. {B} brings a big bucket of water.
bubble: "I'm hot!" says {A}. {B} pours the whole bucket on their head.
example: I'm hot. Let's open the window.

options: I hot. Can I have a cold drink?
I'm hot. Can I have a cold drink?
I have hot. Can I have a cold drink?
practice.why: We use "I'm hot" to talk about how we feel.

meaning_en: you feel afraid
scene: {A} hears a noise at night. {B} comes out from under the bed, in a superhero cape, and shakes.
bubble: "I'm scared!" cries {A}. {B} says, "Me too, but I look cool."

options: I have scared of the dark.

meaning_en: you say your age
scene: {A} meets a tortoise that wears a birthday hat. {B} counts the candles and drops the cake.
bubble: "I'm six years old," says {A}. "I'm one hundred," says the tortoise.

practice.why: We use "be" to say our age: I'm seven.

meaning_en: you tell people your name
meaning_es: dices tu nombre a la gente
scene: {A} gives a speech to a goat. {B} puts a sign on the goat that reads "Lucy".
bubble: "My name's Lucy," says {A}. "Mine's Billy," says the goat.

practice.why: "My name's" is a short way to say "My name is".

meaning_en: you ask for someone's name
scene: {A} meets an alien with five eyes at the bus stop. {B} offers it a banana and a clipboard.
bubble: "What's your name?" "Zlorp," says the alien. {B} writes "Bob".

options: What your name is? I'm Sara.
practice.why: We ask "What's your name?" to know a name.

meaning_en: a friendly phrase when you meet someone new
meaning_es: una frase amable al conocer a alguien
scene: {A} shakes hands with a robot dog. {B} watches as the dog shakes back, and then both arms fall off.
bubble: "Nice to meet you," says {A}. The dog drops a paw.

options: Nice to meet you. I'm Kate.
practice.why: We say "Nice to meet you" the first time.

meaning_en: you say goodbye until the next day
scene: {A} waves at {B} from the school bus, but the bus drives away with {B} on it too.
bubble: "See you tomorrow!" shouts {A}. {B} shouts back from the same bus.

options: Goodbye! See you tomorrow at school.
practice.why: We use "tomorrow" for the next day.

meaning_en: a word to say bye
scene: {A} leaves a party and says goodbye to everyone, even to the plants and the chairs. {B} waves from the sofa.
bubble: "Goodbye!" says {A} to the cactus. The cactus doesn't answer.

practice.why: "Goodbye" is the word we use when we leave.

meaning_en: you say it before sleeping
scene: {A} hugs ten teddy bears and a goldfish bowl. {B} tucks them all in and turns off the light.
bubble: "Good night!" whispers {B}. The goldfish says "Blub."

options: Good night, Mum! See you in the morning.
practice.why: We say "Good night" when someone goes to bed.

meaning_en: you say it on someone's birthday
meaning_es: lo dices en el cumpleaños de alguien
scene: {A} blows out candles and the whole cake flies away. {B} runs after it with a spoon.
bubble: "Happy birthday!" shouts {B}, chasing the cake down the street.

options: Happy birth day to you, Anna!
practice.why: We say "Happy birthday" on the day.

meaning_en: you say it when you give something
scene: {A} hands {B} a plate with a very tiny cake. {B} puts on glasses to see it.
bubble: "Here you are," says {A}. "Where?" asks {B}, looking at the table.
example: Here you are. This is your pencil.

options: Here are you. It's your juice.
Here you is. It's your juice.
Here you are. It's your juice.
practice.why: We say "Here you are" when we give something.

meaning_en: you ask to use something for a short time
meaning_es: pides usar algo por un rato
scene: {A} has no pencil, but a bag full of crayons and a pet frog. {B} holds a very small pencil.
bubble: "Can I borrow your pencil?" {B} gives a tiny stub. {A} sighs.

options: Can I borrow to your pencil?
practice.why: "Borrow" means to take for a short time.

meaning_en: you ask who owns something
scene: {A} finds a giant red shoe in the classroom. {B} looks around the room and sees a clown.
bubble: "Whose is this?" asks {A}. The clown hides behind a plant.

meaning_en: you say something belongs to you
scene: {A} and {B} both hold a toy dinosaur and pull in different directions. The dinosaur looks nervous.
bubble: "It's mine!" "No, it's mine!" The dinosaur says, "It's mine!"

options: It's mine! I got it for my birthday.

meaning_en: you say something belongs to the other person
meaning_es: dices que algo es de la otra persona
scene: {A} finds a huge golden key. {B} points at the lock on the tree and winks.
bubble: "It's yours," says {A}, giving the key. The tree opens its mouth.
example: It's yours. I have my own.

meaning_en: you ask someone to give you a part
meaning_es: pides que te den una parte
scene: {A} has a pizza the size of a table. {B} stands with a small plate and puppy eyes.
bubble: "Share with me!" says {B}. {A} puts one tiny slice on the plate.

meaning_en: each person plays one after the other
meaning_es: cada persona juega una después de otra
scene: {A} and {B} both want the swing. A seagull sits in it and does not move. It wants a turn too.
bubble: "Take turns!" says the teacher. The seagull goes first.
example: We take turns on the slide.

options: We take turn on the slide.
We taking turns on the slide.

meaning_en: you ask people to stand one behind the other
meaning_es: pides que se pongan en fila
scene: {A} leads a line of ducks to the classroom door. {B} counts twelve ducks, and one is a rubber duck.
bubble: "Line up, please!" quack the ducks. The rubber duck squeaks.
example: Line up, please. It's break time.

options: Line on, please. It's break time.
Line up, please. The bell is ringing.
Lining up, please. It's break time.
practice.why: "Line up" means to stand in a line.

meaning_en: you ask for silence
scene: {A} plays the drums in the library. {B}, the librarian, hands over big headphones and a sign.
bubble: "Be quiet, please!" whispers {B}. {A} plays the drums very gently.
example: Be quiet, please. The baby is asleep.

options: Are quiet, please. The baby is asleep.
Be quietly, please. The baby is asleep.
Be quiet, please. The film is starting.
practice.why: After "Be" we use an adjective, not an adverb.

meaning_en: you raise your hand to speak
scene: {A} knows the answer and jumps so high that a lamp breaks. {B} calmly puts their hand up.
bubble: "Put your hand up!" says the teacher. {A} puts both feet up.
example: Put your hand up if you know.

options: Put your hand in if you know.
Put your hand up to ask a question.
Put up your hands down if you know.
practice.why: We say "put your hand up" to ask for a turn.

meaning_en: you ask someone to shut the door
scene: {A} stands in the rain with a bucket on his head. {B} holds the handle and looks at a puddle in the hall.
bubble: "Close the door!" says {B}. A wet dog runs in anyway.

practice.why: "Close" is an action verb. We use it with a door.

meaning_en: you make the light work
scene: {A} walks in the dark room and falls over a sleeping cat. {B} walks in with a big torch.
bubble: "Switch on the light!" Click! The cat is wearing a hat.

practice.why: "Switch on" means to make something start.

meaning_en: you remove writing from the board
meaning_es: quitas lo escrito de la pizarra
scene: {A} cleans the board with a big sock. {B} watches as a drawing of a cat becomes a drawing of a big elephant.
bubble: "Clean the board!" says the teacher. {A} cleans it with a banana.

meaning_en: you take something from the floor
scene: {A} drops a pencil, and it rolls away down a hill. {B} runs after it in pyjamas.
bubble: "Pick up the pencil!" shouts {A}. It rolls into a pond.

options: Pick the pencil up of, please.
practice.why: "Pick up" means to take from the floor.

meaning_en: you make a drawing
scene: {A} draws a horse with six legs. {B} looks closely and says it looks like a spider.
bubble: "Draw a picture!" says the teacher. {A} draws the teacher with a tail.
example: Draw a picture of your family.

options: Draw a picture off your family.
Do a picture of your family.
Draw a picture of a dog.
practice.why: We say "draw a picture", not "do a picture".

meaning_en: you fill a shape with colour
scene: {A} paints a star yellow. A real star falls from the sky and says, "Thanks, it's perfect."
bubble: "Colour the star!" says {B}. {A} also paints a cloud and a cat.

practice.why: "Colour" is a verb; no preposition is needed.

meaning_en: you use scissors on paper
scene: {A} cuts a big paper into forty tiny pieces. {B} walks in, thinks it is snow, and throws it around.
bubble: "Cut the paper!" says {B}. {A} cuts a hole in the table too.

meaning_en: you say numbers from one to ten
meaning_es: dices los números del uno al diez
scene: {A} counts to ten, but gets stuck after seven. {B} whispers eight, nine, ten from behind a curtain.
bubble: "Count to ten!" says {B}. "One... two... lunch?" says {A}.

practice.why: "Count to" + number is the right pattern.

meaning_en: you put your name on paper
meaning_es: pones tu nombre en el papel
scene: {A} writes their name on a wall with a banana. {B} brings a bucket of paint.
bubble: "Write your name!" says the teacher. {A} writes it on the board, upside down.
example: Write your name on the page.

options: Write you name on the page.
Write the name your on the page.
practice.why: "Your" shows that the name belongs to you.

meaning_en: you read a short tale
scene: {A} reads a story to a very sleepy dog. {B} listens and puts a blanket on the dog.
bubble: "Read the story!" says {B}. The dog snores before the dragon comes.
example: Read the story to the class.

options: Reads the story to the class.
Read story the to the class.
practice.why: The verb "read" is the same in imperative.

meaning_en: you show with your finger
scene: {A} points at the cat. The cat points at the fish. The fish points at {B}.
bubble: "Point to the cat!" says {B}. Everyone points at the wrong animal.
example: Point to the cat in the picture.

options: Point at to the cat, please.
practice.why: We say "point to" something to show it.

meaning_en: you ask someone to let you see something
meaning_es: le pides a alguien que te deje ver algo
scene: {A} puts a mystery box on the table. {B} bites a nail and stands on a chair.
bubble: "Show me!" says {B}. {A} opens the box: it is full of socks.

options: Show to me your drawing, please.

meaning_en: you say it before sharing news
meaning_es: lo dices antes de contar una noticia
scene: {A} runs in with a huge grin, covered in paint. {B} puts the cup down and waits.
bubble: "Guess what!" says {A}. "You are blue," says {B}.
example: Guess what! I have a puppy.

options: Guessing what! I have a puppy.
Guess it what! I have a puppy.

meaning_en: you ask to look or think
scene: {A} holds a tiny photo of a camel. {B} puts a magnifying glass over it.
bubble: "Let me see." {B} looks for an hour. It is a very small camel.

options: Let me to see your photo.
practice.why: After "let me" we use the base verb.

meaning_en: you want people to watch you
scene: {A} balances on a ball with a spoon on their nose. {B} counts the seconds.
bubble: "Look at me!" shouts {A}. The ball rolls and they fall into the pool.

options: Look to me! I can jump!
Look at me! I can jump!

meaning_en: you say it before doing something
meaning_es: lo dices antes de hacer algo
scene: {A} stands next to a trampoline. {B} holds a stopwatch, ready to record the world's longest jump.
bubble: "Watch this!" Boing! {A} lands on the roof. {B} gives ten out of ten.
example: Watch this! I can do a cartwheel.

options: Watch this! I can ride my bike.
Watch to this! I can ride my bike.
Watching this! I can ride my bike.
practice.why: "Watch" is a verb; no preposition is needed.

bubble: "Too many!" shouts {B}. {A} eats five more.

practice.why: We use "too many" with plural nouns.

meaning_en: more than needed (uncountable)
scene: {A} puts too much sugar in the tea. The spoon stands up on its own. {B} calls it "tea cake".
bubble: "Too much sugar!" says {B}. The spoon agrees.

meaning_en: as much as you need
scene: {A} serves a plate of rice. {B} asks for more, and more, and more. The cook cries, "Enough!"
bubble: "Enough!" says the cook. {B} says, "A bit more."

options: Do you have food enough, of?

meaning_en: one with the other
scene: {A} and {B} give each other a hug, then a high five, then a sandwich. The sandwich falls.

practice.why: "Each other" shows two people do the same.

meaning_en: alone, without help
scene: {A} builds a sandcastle alone, with only a cat, a dog and {B} watching. Nobody believes {A}.

example: I can tie my shoes by myself.

options: I can tie my shoes by me.
I can wash my hands by myself.
I can wash my hands myself by.

meaning_en: you say a strong no
scene: {A} asks a crocodile, "Do you like dentists?" The crocodile closes its mouth and says "Of course not."
bubble: "Of course not!" says the crocodile. {B} drops the toothbrush.

meaning_en: you agree with a negative sentence
meaning_es: estás de acuerdo con una frase negativa
scene: {A} says, "I don't like broccoli." {B} says, "Me neither." The broccoli says, "I heard that."
bubble: "Me neither," says {B}. The broccoli cries.

practice.why: "Me neither" agrees with a negative sentence.

meaning_en: you have the same experience
scene: {A} sneezes, {B} sneezes, and the cat sneezes. All three say "Same here" and sneeze again.
bubble: "Same here!" says {B}, with a tissue.

scene: {A} eats ten tacos, and then feels very ill. {B} gives {A} a glass of water and a comfy cushion.
bubble: "Never again!" groans {A}. Tomorrow, {A} has ten tacos.

options: I'll again never eat ten tacos.
Never again am I eat ten tacos.

scene: {A} sees dark clouds. {B} runs, with an umbrella, a bag and a dog. The dog runs faster than the bag.
bubble: "Hurry home!" says {A}. Splash! Rain starts.

meaning_en: you wish someone a good sleep
meaning_es: le deseas a alguien un buen sueño
scene: {A} tucks a teddy bear in. The bear says, "Sweet dreams" and falls asleep first. {B} turns off the lamp.
bubble: "Sweet dreams!" whispers {A}. The bear snores.

meaning_en: you comb your hair
scene: {A} brushes their hair with a broom. {B} watches as a bird builds a nest in it.
bubble: "Brush your hair!" says {B}. The bird says, "Please don't."

meaning_es: le pides a alguien que juegue contigo
scene: {A} holds a ball and a frog. {B} hides behind a plant. The frog says, "I'll play with you."
bubble: "Play with me!" says {A}. The frog hops away.

meaning_es: le pides a alguien que te pase la pelota
scene: {A} stands alone in goal. {B} holds the ball and looks at a butterfly. The ball rolls away alone.
bubble: "Pass me the ball!" shouts {A}. {B} passes a butterfly.

meaning_es: golpeas la pelota con el pie

bubble: "Kick the ball!" says {B}. {A} kicks a shoe instead.

options: Kick to the ball to me.
Kick the ball into the goal.
practice.why: "Kick" means to hit with your foot.

meaning_es: lanzas la pelota con la mano
scene: {A} throws the ball to a dog, but the dog throws it back. They keep going for an hour.
bubble: "Throw the ball!" says {A}. The dog says, "Your turn."

options: Throw to the ball to Tom.

meaning_en: you take the ball in your hands
meaning_es: atrapas la pelota con las manos

example: Catch the ball with two hands.

options: Catch to the ball with two hands.
Catches the ball with two hands.
practice.why: "Catch" means to take something in the air.

meaning_en: you put the ball in the goal
scene: {A} scores a goal, then another goal, then one in the wrong net. {B} the goalkeeper has fallen asleep.
bubble: "Score a goal!" says {B}. {A} scores in the bin.
example: He scores a goal every match.

options: He makes a goal every match.
He does a goal every match.

options: We want to earn the game.

Make a go at this game.

practice.why: "Give me five" is a friendly gesture.

scene: {A} makes a face like a fish. {B} makes a face like a potato. The teacher makes a face like a teacher.
bubble: "Make a face!" says {B}. Everyone makes a funny face.

options: Make a deep breath and relax.
Take a deeply breath and relax.
Take a deep breath, then jump.

meaning_en: you clean the car with water

bubble: "Wash the car!" says {B}. {A} washes the dog too.
example: We wash the car on Sunday.

options: We washing the car on Sunday.
We washed the car with sunday.

He can to climb a tree.

options: Pick up a flower for Mum from.
Pick off a flower for Mum.
I pick a flower in the garden.

options: Planting a seed in the soil.
We plant a seed at the water.
We plant a seed in spring.

options: We eat the ducks in the park.
We feeds the ducks in the park.

meaning_en: you take care of someone or something
scene: {A} looks after a baby elephant. The elephant looks after {A} too, with a huge hat. {B} brings a book.

options: I look at my little brother, he is sick.
I look for my little brother, he is sick.
practice.why: "Look after" means to take care of.
